note: Recorded by the perf job in .github/workflows/ci.yml, which prints the number to commit here. Throughput is per CPU-second, not wall clock, so a busy shared runner does not read as a regression. A number measured on any other machine class is not comparable; scripts/check_perf_budget.py fails rather than compares while rowsPerCpuSecond is null.
memoryMeasuredOn: CPython 3.13.9, tracemalloc peak over a full run() of a 10,000-trip synthetic feed. CPython 3.12.14 measures 30.53x on the same feed, a 1.01x spread, so the 1.03x budget covers both supported interpreters with room and still catches a regression as small as one retained tuple per row (measured at 1.05x). Unlike rowsPerCpuSecond this number is not machine-class specific: tracemalloc counts bytes requested from Python, not resident set size. Before the per-file value pool landed the same feed measured 36.62x (3.12) and 37.02x (3.13). See scripts/check_memory_budget.py and FIX-04.
